meta.title: From Day One to Competent: Supporting the Store Manager at the Pivot Point
meta.subtitle: A joined-up proposal for visibility, coaching, onboarding, and repeatable store execution across 120 APAC stores

slides.title: From Day One to Competent
slides.subtitle: Supporting RetailCo store managers with Spacesight, Echo, Harbor Wiki, and Alivia
slides.script: We are looking at RetailCo through the eyes of the store manager, because that is where head office intent meets the shop floor. Today, that manager is expected to coach new hires, lift sales standards, explain performance gaps, and coordinate rosters with limited live support. Our proposal follows one new frontline hire from their first day to the point where they can perform with confidence. As that journey unfolds, we will show where Spacesight, Echo, Harbor Wiki, and Alivia fit together as one operating system for better store execution.

slides.title: The end state: every new hire has the best manager beside them
slides.subtitle: We start with what good looks like, then work backward to how RetailCo gets there.
slides.script: We want to start at the end, because the destination matters. A new hire should not have to hope the right person is working that day. A store manager should not have to rely on memory, instinct, or a Monday spreadsheet to know what is happening. Head office should be able to see patterns across 120 stores without flattening local judgement. Good looks like a manager with live signals, proven plays, and a shared language for coaching every associate from day one.

slides.title: What good looks like from the store manager’s chair

cards.heading: The new hire knows what to do
cards.body: They learn from proven answers, examples, and store routines captured in Harbor Wiki.

cards.heading: The manager knows where to coach
cards.body: Spacesight and Echo reveal floor behavior and customer conversations while they still matter.

cards.heading: The COO sees the system working
cards.body: Alivia packages the evidence, priorities, and rollout plan into one joined-up proposal.

slides.script: From the manager’s chair, the end state is practical. The new hire can ask, search, and learn from what RetailCo’s strongest people already do, not just from whoever is nearby. The manager can see where traffic is building, where service is slipping, and what customers are actually hearing. The COO can stop managing through delayed summaries and start seeing patterns while they are still actionable. Alivia then turns those findings into a proposal that RetailCo can review, refine, and scale deliberately rather than as disconnected tools.

slides.quote: My best store managers outsell my worst ones by 3x. I cannot bottle what they do.
slides.script: This is the heart of the opportunity. RetailCo already has excellence inside the business, but it is trapped in individual managers, individual shifts, and individual stores. When the best managers outsell the worst ones by 3x, the answer is not only more training. The answer is to observe what great execution looks like, hear how great conversations sound, and convert that into a living source of guidance. That is why we connect Spacesight for behavior, Echo for conversations, and Harbor Wiki for repeatable know-how.

slides.title: Day one: remove the lottery from onboarding
slides.subtitle: The new hire’s first shift should not depend entirely on who happens to be working.
slides.script: Now we move back to day one. RetailCo told us onboarding takes six weeks and depends entirely on whoever happens to be working that day. From a manager’s perspective, that creates two problems at once. The new hire learns inconsistently, and the manager has to keep repeating the basics while still running the floor. We would use Harbor Wiki as the front door for store knowledge, then feed it with the behaviors and conversations that Spacesight and Echo help identify as worth copying.

slides.title: Each operational pain gets an owner

rows.right: Spacesight shows floor activity before last week becomes history.
Echo and Spacesight identify the habits behind stronger managers.
Harbor Wiki turns proven routines into searchable guidance for new hires.
Open workstream: Alivia scopes scheduling integration and workflow requirements.

slides.script: We are being explicit about ownership because every pain should either map to a product or be called out honestly. The Monday visibility problem is directly addressed by Spacesight, with Echo adding what customers and associates actually say. The 3x manager gap is addressed by finding the behaviors and conversations that explain better execution, then turning them into reusable content in Harbor Wiki. The six-week onboarding challenge is a Harbor Wiki use case. Scheduling is different: these products do not automatically generate rosters, so Alivia should capture it as an open workflow and integration workstream.

slides.title: The first week shifts from shadowing to guided practice

rows.left: New hire waits for ad hoc explanations
rows.right: Harbor Wiki gives consistent answers and store routines.

rows.left: Customer talk is invisible after the shift
rows.right: Echo captures and scores real frontline conversations.
Examples become reusable guidance for the next hire.

slides.script: In the first week, we are not trying to replace the store manager. We are trying to give that manager leverage. Today, shadowing can be useful, but it is fragile because it depends on who is present and what they remember to explain. With Harbor Wiki, the new hire has a consistent baseline. With Spacesight, the manager can coach from what happened on the floor. With Echo, coaching can include how associates explain, recommend, and respond to customers. The result is guided practice rather than informal absorption.

slides.title: From competent in one store to consistent across 120
slides.subtitle: Once the first hire learns faster, RetailCo can scale the same operating rhythm.
slides.script: Once a new hire becomes competent, the question changes. We are no longer asking whether one person learned the job. We are asking how RetailCo repeats that outcome across 120 APAC stores and 2,000 frontline staff. This is where the manager remains the pivot. We give them signals, language, and reusable plays, while head office gains a clearer picture of what is working. The objective is not central control for its own sake; it is making the best local execution easier to copy.

slides.title: What becomes repeatable
slides.subtitle: The manager’s best work becomes a system, not a personal workaround.
bullets: Proposal and rollout packaging through Alivia
slides.script: What becomes repeatable is the combination, not any single product in isolation. Spacesight helps the manager and COO see what is happening on the shop floor without waiting for a Monday spreadsheet. Echo makes customer conversations coachable instead of anecdotal. Harbor Wiki bottles the routines, answers, and manager plays that explain stronger performance. Alivia then packages the evidence, scope, open scheduling workstream, and rollout path into a proposal RetailCo can actually decide on. That is how one new hire’s journey becomes an operating model.

slides.title: Waiting another quarter means another quarter of unbottled execution
slides.subtitle: The smallest first step is a focused pilot that proves the manager workflow before scale.
bullets: Run Spacesight, Echo, and Harbor Wiki together
Document scheduling requirements as an open workstream
Use Alivia to produce the scale proposal
slides.script: If RetailCo waits another quarter, the cost is not an invented percentage on a spreadsheet. It is another quarter where head office learns about last week on Monday, another quarter where the best managers keep outperforming without being bottled, another quarter where new hires learn by chance, and another quarter where roster coordination remains a manual burden. Our smallest sensible first step is three representative stores. We run Spacesight, Echo, and Harbor Wiki together, document the scheduling workflow honestly, and use Alivia to turn the evidence into a scale proposal.

approach.angle: Take the store manager's point of view. They are the pivot between what head office wants and what actually happens, and today they are unsupported.
approach.device: Follow one new hire from day one to competent, letting the products appear as they are needed.
approach.opener: Open on the end state - show them what good looks like, then explain how.
approach.close: Close on what they lose by waiting another quarter, then propose the smallest first step.
